description: Each gender's volume is its number of invoices. Every invoice counts, including several invoices on the same order.

c.request: Going from invoices to their orders and on to the customers (skip anything that doesn't link up), how many invoiced orders does each customer gender (`Customers.gender`) have? Turn that into each gender's share of the overall total, and list the genders whose share is above the average share across genders: give the gender, the count, the share, and how far the share sits above the average. Don't round anything. Each gender's volume is its number of invoices. Every invoice counts, including several invoices on the same order.
c.sql: WITH invoice_counts_by_gender AS (SELECT c.gender, COUNT(i.invoice_number) as invoice_count FROM Invoices i JOIN Orders o ON i.order_id = o.order_id JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.gender), total_invoices AS (SELECT SUM(invoice_count) as total FROM invoice_counts_by_gender), stats_with_avg AS (SELECT icbg.gender, icbg.invoice_count, CAST(icbg.invoice_count AS DECIMAL(19,4)) / (SELECT total FROM total_invoices) as share, CAST(1 AS DECIMAL(19,4)) / CAST(COUNT(*) OVER () AS DECIMAL(19,4)) as avg_share FROM invoice_counts_by_gender icbg) SELECT gender, invoice_count, share, share - avg_share as above_average FROM stats_with_avg WHERE share > avg_share

d.request: Count the total invoices per customer gender (where each invoice counts separately even if multiple invoices originate from the same order), calculate each gender's proportion of all invoices, identify genders whose proportion exceeds the average proportion across all genders, and report the gender, invoice count, proportion, and excess above the average proportion.
d.sql: WITH invoice_by_gender AS (SELECT c.gender, COUNT(i.invoice_number) as invoice_count FROM Customers c JOIN Orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN Invoices i ON o.order_id = i.order_id WHERE c.gender IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.gender), with_stats AS (SELECT gender, invoice_count, CAST(invoice_count AS DECIMAL(19,4)) / SUM(CAST(invoice_count AS DECIMAL(19,4))) OVER () as proportion, 1.0 / COUNT(*) OVER () as avg_proportion FROM invoice_by_gender) SELECT gender, invoice_count, proportion, proportion - avg_proportion as excess FROM with_stats WHERE proportion > avg_proportion ORDER BY gender;

b.request: Group invoices by customer gender, count the number of invoices per gender, calculate each gender's share of total invoices, compute the average share across all genders, and report each gender with an above-average share along with its invoice count, exact share value, and exact amount by which the share exceeds the average.
b.sql: WITH invoice_counts_by_gender AS (SELECT c.gender, COUNT(i.invoice_number) as invoice_count FROM Invoices i JOIN Orders o ON i.order_id = o.order_id JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.gender), total_invoices AS (SELECT SUM(invoice_count) as total FROM invoice_counts_by_gender), gender_shares AS (SELECT icg.gender, icg.invoice_count, icg.invoice_count / CAST(ti.total AS DECIMAL(19,4)) as share FROM invoice_counts_by_gender icg CROSS JOIN total_invoices ti), average_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) as avg_share FROM gender_shares) SELECT gs.gender, gs.invoice_count, gs.share, gs.share - av.avg_share as share_excess FROM gender_shares gs CROSS JOIN average_share av WHERE gs.share > av.avg_share ORDER BY gs.share DESC
b.raw: Group invoices by customer gender, count the number of invoices per gender, calculate each gender's share of total invoices, compute the average share across all genders, and report each gender with an above-average share along with its invoice count, exact share value, and exact amount by which the share exceeds the average.

a.request: Linking each invoice to its order and that order's customer (dropping invoices without a matching order or customer), count for each customer gender (`Customers.gender`) the number of invoices, counting every invoice even when an order has several. Work out each gender's share as its count divided by the total of the counts over all genders, and average these shares across the genders. Return only the genders whose share is above that average, showing the gender, the count, the share, and the share minus the average share, without rounding.
a.sql:
WITH gender_invoice_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    c.gender,
    COUNT(i.invoice_number) as invoice_count
  FROM Invoices i
  INNER JOIN Orders o ON i.order_id = o.order_id
  INNER JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  GROUP BY c.gender
),
totals AS (
  SELECT 
    SUM(invoice_count) as total_count
  FROM gender_invoice_counts
),
shares_calculated AS (
  SELECT 
    gic.gender,
    gic.invoice_count,
    CAST(gic.invoice_count AS DECIMAL(19,4)) / t.total_count as share
  FROM gender_invoice_counts gic
  CROSS JOIN totals t
),
average_share_calc AS (
  SELECT 
    AVG(share) as avg_share
  FROM shares_calculated
)
SELECT 
  sc.gender,
  sc.invoice_count as count,
  sc.share,
  sc.share - asc.avg_share as share_minus_avg
FROM shares_calculated sc
CROSS JOIN average_share_calc asc
WHERE sc.share > asc.avg_share
ORDER BY sc.gender
